question: In June 2021, the Ministry of Heavy Industries increased the subsidy for electric two-wheelers to ______ per kWh under the FAME India Scheme Phase II.
solution:
The correct answer is__** ₹15,000.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Under the FAME India Scheme Phase II, the Ministry of Heavy Industries increased the subsidy for electric two-wheelers to 15,000 per kWh in June 2021.**
 
• The Central government has increased the subsidy under the** second phase of the FAME India scheme on electric two-wheelers by 50 percent.**
 
• The subsidy will now be** Rs 15,000 per kWh for electric two-wheelers under FAME India phase II.** Earlier, it was Rs 10,000 per kWh. In addition, the maximum subsidy for an electric two-wheeler will now be 40% of its cost, up from 20% previously.
 
• The government's continued support of electronic vehicles (EVs) will lower the price of electric two-wheelers, which will be very advantageous to buyers of electric motorcycles and scooters.
 
• Future mobility options must be sustainable, and better incentives for electric two-wheelers will boost adoption and encourage additional domestic technological investments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• ​**Some of the key features of the FAME II scheme are given below.**

 
 
• Allocation of Rs 10,000 crores for a period of 3 years from 2019 to 2022. A budget of Rs 1 billion crore has been set aside to install electric vehicle charging stations.
 
• It has been suggested that every electric bus receive one slow charging unit and every ten electric buses receive one fast charging station.
 
• The purchase of about 5 lakh three-wheelers, 7000 electric buses, and 35,000 four-wheelers will be encouraged by the central government.
 
• FAME India Scheme's official website is located at https://fame2.heavyindustry.gov.in/. The Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises is in charge of overseeing the program.
